title: Epic: Hardware tuning profiles pack (kernel + scheduling + memory) for H100/B200/L40S
creator: Mateo Alvarez
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Goal
Deliver a vetted, versioned “hardware tuning profiles pack” for Redwood’s serving runtime that selects the best-known runtime configuration per GPU SKU and workload shape. Profiles must be observable, reversible, and safe to roll out in Hosted, with controlled opt-in/pinning for Dedicated and clear guidance for Private.

Why this matters
We are increasingly shipping across heterogeneous GPU pools (H100, L40S, early B200). Today, runtime defaults drift and perf behavior becomes hard to reason about across regions/driver baselines. A versioned profile pack makes performance behavior repeatable and enables SRE/Infra + customer-facing teams to communicate expectations and safely roll forward/back.

In scope
- Runtime tuning knobs: kernel selection/variants, scheduler/batching heuristics, KV cache + allocator settings, prefill/decode prioritization, concurrency limits.
- Host/container recommendations where we control them: CPU pinning/NUMA guidance, hugepages, CUDA env vars (separate “required” vs “best-effort” by deployment mode).
- Reproducible benchmark protocol + acceptance thresholds per SKU integrated into benchmark-lab / perf-canary.
- Observability required to validate expected behavior: per-stage latency, queueing time, kernel fallback counters, OOM/fragmentation signals, profile_id adoption.

Non-goals
- Rewriting kernels from scratch for every model family (kernel work is incremental and targeted).
- Bespoke customer configs (support overrides but with guardrails + auditability).

Deliverables
1) Profile pack artifact
- Config schema + validation (JSON/YAML loader)
- Per-SKU defaults (H100/L40S; provisional B200)
- Versioning + compatibility rules (SKU/driver/CUDA/MIG)
- Deterministic selection and override precedence (fleet default → control plane pin → customer override) with guardrails

2) Docs (Confluence)
- Overview and ownership
- Profile schema + selection rules
- Expected behavior: H100, L40S, B200 preview
- Benchmarking matrix + acceptance thresholds
- Rollout/runbook + troubleshooting
- ADR: where selection logic lives, rollback strategy, override policy

3) CI/perf gating
- Profile correctness checks (schema validation + golden snapshots)
- Benchmark matrix runner persisted with profile_version tags
- Perf-canary gates for default profile changes

Milestones (targeting runtime-1.22)
M0 (Done): Kickoff, scope lock, initial doc skeletons
M1 (In progress): Profile schema + selection implementation behind feature flag; instrumentation for profile_id/sku tags
M2 (Next): Benchmark matrix integrated + acceptance thresholds; initial H100/L40S profiles validated in benchmark-lab
M3 (Next): Hosted canary enablement + SRE guardrails + rollback automation; Dedicated opt-in flow + pinning
M4 (Later): B200 compatibility gate + smoke suite; expand compatibility matrix + MIG/no-MIG handling
M5 (Later): Public-ish internal docs complete (expected behavior tables + troubleshooting)

Rollout plan (high level)
- Hosted: canary cohort (small %) → expand by region/model mix; kill-switch to revert to previous profile_version
- Dedicated: opt-in only for default changes; allow per-customer profile_version pin with guardrails + audit log
- Private: ship default profiles in installer/Helm with warnings for unsupported driver/CUDA; document required vs best-effort host knobs

Open questions / risks to manage (tracked here)
- Compatibility surface: how strict to be on driver/CUDA mismatches (esp. B200 early fleet). Current direction: hard gate for unsafe combinations; allow explicit pin/override only with “ack” and clear logging.
- Tail latency under mixed workloads: ensure scheduler bucket defaults are safe; perf-canary must block p99 regressions beyond SRE thresholds.
- Memory headroom/fragmentation: compaction thresholds + allocator knobs must include guardrails to prevent sustained fragmentation and OOM oscillation.
- Cardinality: profile_id + sku tags are required; ensure metrics map keeps cardinality bounded (labels must not include model_id in high-cardinality histograms unless sampled).

Definition of done (for v1 in runtime-1.22)
- Profile pack loads + validates; selection deterministic and logged at startup and model-load time
- H100 and L40S expected behavior documented and validated against benchmark-lab results
- Hosted canary completed with SLO guardrails + rollback playbook exercised
- Dedicated opt-in and profile_version pin supported with auditability
- B200 bring-up gated with compatibility checks + smoke suite; documented as “preview” expectations
